image_description: A large, mature common iguana (Iguana iguana) resting on the ground amidst leaf litter and low-lying vegetation. The iguana has a robust body with greyish-green coloration and distinct orange/reddish hues on its lower jaw and limbs. It features a prominent dorsal crest of spine-like scales running from the neck down the back. The head is large and triangular with visible granular scales and a subtympanic shield. The tail extends behind it, partially obscured by foliage.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible, exhibiting the characteristic triangular shape and large size relative to the body. A dewlap structure is visible under the chin/jaw area.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the eye socket and general eye shape are visible, the resolution and lighting prevent clear identification of 'round pupils' and specifically 'golden irises'. The eye appears dark/shadowed rather than distinctly golden.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: A large circular subtympanic shield (scale) is present below the tympanum.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct, large, circular scale pattern is visible on the side of the head, consistent with the location and appearance of a subtympanic shield.
The torso is thick and muscular, fitting the description of a robust body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Coloration is bright green in juveniles, becoming darker green to greyish-green in adults with broad black bands on the body and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The iguana displays adult coloration: primarily greyish-green with some darker banding on the tail and body, plus orange accents on the limbs/jaw. This matches the adult phase description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Row of enlarged, spine-like scales running from the nape along the midline of the back to the tail base, forming a serrated crest.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A very prominent, continuous row of spine-like scales (dorsal crest) runs from the neck down the spine. This is a defining feature and is clearly present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in small, granular scales with larger, plate-like scales on the head.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture of the skin shows fine granularity on the body and larger, smoother plate-like structures on the head/face area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are long and muscular with five clawed digits on each foot.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front left limb is visible and appears muscular, but the feet/digits are largely obscured by leaves and shadow. It is impossible to definitively count 'five clawed digits' or verify the anatomy of all four limbs due to occlusion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and longer than body, used for balance and defense.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible extending backwards, but it disappears into the background foliage before its full length can be measured against the body. Therefore, verifying it is 'longer than the body' is not strictly testable from this single view.

The right hind leg seems to merge indistinctly with the ground and shadows. The anatomical connection of the foot to the leg is unclear, suggesting potential structural ambiguity or fusion with the environment.
